original_text:
Plant Cells
Most organelles and other cell structures are common to all eukaryotic cells
Plants have 3 additional structures important to their function:
Cell wall
Central vacuole
Plastid
Plants synthesize their own C-molecules (sugar) directly from CO2and water in the environment through a process called photosynthesis
explanation: While most organelles are common to all eukaryotic cells, plant cells contain three unique and essential structures: the cell wall, the central vacuole, and plastids. Plants are autotrophic, meaning they synthesize their own carbon-containing organic molecules (sugars) directly from inorganic carbon dioxide and water in their environment via the process of photosynthesis.

questions.q: What are the three additional structures important to plant cell function that are not typically found in animal cells?
opts: Cell wall, Central vacuole, and Plastid
questions.exp: The slide lists the three additional structures in plant cells as the cell wall, central vacuole, and plastid.

questions.q: How do plants obtain carbon-containing molecules (sugars)?
opts: By absorbing them directly from soil nutrients
By synthesizing them from carbon dioxide and water through photosynthesis
By breaking down fatty acids in peroxisomes
questions.exp: Plants synthesize their own carbon molecules (sugar) directly from CO2 and water in the environment through photosynthesis.
